events.title: Battle of Princeton
events.description: George Washington's Continental Army defeated British forces near Princeton, New Jersey, days after the victory at Trenton. Washington led a surprise night march around Cornwallis's army to attack the British rear guard.
events.significance: Together with the victory at Trenton, it revived American morale and the Patriot cause after a string of defeats, and forced the British to withdraw from much of New Jersey.

events.title: Alaska Admitted as the 49th U.S. State
events.description: President Dwight D. Eisenhower signed the proclamation formally admitting Alaska to the Union, making it the 49th state.
events.significance: Alaska became the largest U.S. state by area, adding vast natural resources and strategic Arctic territory to the nation. Hawaii followed as the 50th state later in 1959.

events.title: Martin Luther Excommunicated
events.description: Pope Leo X issued the papal bull Decet Romanum Pontificem, formally excommunicating Martin Luther from the Catholic Church after he refused to recant his criticisms of church practices.
events.significance: The excommunication cemented the break between Luther and Rome and propelled the Protestant Reformation, which reshaped religion and politics across Europe.

events.title: United States Severs Diplomatic Relations with Cuba
events.description: President Eisenhower announced the end of diplomatic relations with Cuba amid worsening tensions following Fidel Castro's revolution, nationalizations of American property, and Cuba's growing alignment with the Soviet Union.
events.significance: The break set the stage for the Bay of Pigs invasion and the Cuban Missile Crisis, and began decades of hostility and the U.S. embargo.

events.title: START II Treaty Signed
events.description: U.S. President George H. W. Bush and Russian President Boris Yeltsin signed the Treaty on Further Reduction and Limitation of Strategic Offensive Arms (START II) in Moscow.
events.significance: The treaty aimed to cut deployed strategic nuclear warheads by roughly two-thirds and ban multiple-warhead land-based missiles, marking a major post-Cold War arms control effort, though it never fully entered into force.
